days.goalUz: Işlatiladi: inversion (Never / Rarely / Not only / No sooner / Only when / Under no circumstances) — dalilni baholaş, munozara va argumentativ esse.

sections.titleUz: Öqiş: “Aqlli odamlar nega yolğon sarlavhaga işonadi”

exercises.explanationUz: bias — tarafkaşlik.
exercises.question: What does “bias” mean?

exercises.explanationUz: Seldom + have + ega + V3.
exercises.question: Seldom ___ such a detailed report.

exercises.explanationUz: No sooner had … than.
exercises.text: No sooner had he published the post ___ people started criticising it.

exercises.explanationUz: Not until + vaqt, keyin asosiy gapda inversion: did they realise.
exercises.question: Which sentence is correct?
options: Not until the next day they realised the mistake.
Not until the next day did they realise the mistake.
Not until the next day they did realise the mistake.
Not until the next day realised they the mistake.

exercises.instructionUz: Gapni ingliz tiliga inversion bilan tarjima qiling.
exercises.explanationUz: “Heç qaçon … magan edim” — Never had I + V3.
exercises.source: Men heç qaçon bunday işonarli nutqni eşitmagan edim.
accepted: Never had I heard such a convincing speech
Never had I heard such a persuasive speech
Never before had I heard such a convincing speech

exercises.explanationUz: Only after + V-ing … + did + ega + fe’l.
evidence — dalil, misleading — çalğituvçi, persuade — köndirmoq, fallacy — mantiqiy xato.

exercises.instructionUz: Grammatik qoida haqidagi fikr töğrimi (true) yoki xatomi (false)?
exercises.explanationUz: Inversion asosan rasmiy va ta’kidli uslubga xos. Fikr töğri.
exercises.statement: Inversion after “Never” or “Rarely” is mainly used in formal or emphatic language.

days.goalUz: Işlatiladi: cleft sentences (It is … that, What … is, All … is, The reason why … is that) — mehnat bozori muammolarini tahlil qiliş va taklifnoma yoziş.

exercises.explanationUz: vacancy — böş iş örni.
exercises.question: What does “vacancy” mean?

exercises.explanationUz: What + ega + fe’l + is …
exercises.question: ___ is better public transport.

exercises.explanationUz: It is / was … that …
exercises.text: It ___ the lack of experience ___ worried the employers.

exercises.explanationUz: The reason … is that …
exercises.question: Which sentence is correct?
options: The reason is because of the cost.
The reason is that it costs too much.
The reason it is that the cost.
The reason is what it costs too much.

exercises.instructionUz: Gapni ingliz tiliga cleft gap bilan tarjima qiling.
exercises.explanationUz: “Menga faqat … kerak” — All I need is …
exercises.source: Menga faqat bir oz vaqt kerak.
accepted: All I need is a little time
All I need is some time
All I need is a bit of time
All that I need is a little time

exercises.explanationUz: What + ega + did + was + fe’l …
employer — iş beruvçi, entrepreneur — tadbirkor, incentive — rağbat, unemployment — işsizlik.

exercises.instructionUz: Grammatik qoida haqidagi fikr töğrimi (true) yoki xatomi (false)?
exercises.explanationUz: Wh-cleft’da “What I need it is …” — ortiqça it. Fikr xato.
exercises.statement: “What I need it is a holiday” is a correct cleft sentence.

days.goalUz: Işlatiladi: impersonal passive (It is said / believed that …, X is thought to be / to have + V3, There are thought to be …) — iqtisodiy yangiliklar va ehtiyotkor hisobot.

sections.titleUz: Öqiş: “Yangi Ipak yöli: umid va şubha”

exercises.explanationUz: tariff — boj.
exercises.question: What does “tariff” mean?

exercises.explanationUz: Hozirgi holat — is said to be.
exercises.question: The new minister ___ very experienced.

exercises.explanationUz: Ötmiş — to have + V3: to have left.
exercises.text: The suspect is believed to ___ ___ (leave) the country last week.

exercises.explanationUz: It is reported that … yoki … is reported to …
exercises.question: Which sentence is correct?
options: The company is reported that it has lost money.
It is reported that the company has lost money.
It is reported the company to have lost money.
The company reported to have lost money.

exercises.explanationUz: “… deb taxmin qilinadi” — It is estimated that …
exercises.source: Eksport ikki baravar oşadi, deb taxmin qilinmoqda.
accepted: It is estimated that exports will double
Exports are estimated to double
Exports are expected to double
It is expected that exports will double

exercises.explanationUz: There + are + thought + to be …
merchant — savdogar, supply chain — ta’minot zanjiri, inflation — inflyatsiya, landlocked — dengizga çiqişi yöq.
“It is said that …” da’voni bildiradi, isbotni emas. Fikr xato.
exercises.statement: “It is said that …” proves that a statement is true.

days.goalUz: Işlatiladi: Mixed Conditionals (ötmiş → hozir, hozir → ötmiş), Had I known … — til, madaniyat va özlik haqida fikr yuritiş.

exercises.explanationUz: bilingual — ikki tilli.
exercises.question: What does “bilingual” mean?

exercises.explanationUz: Ötmiş şart, hozirgi natija: would + be.
exercises.question: If I had accepted that job, I ___ in Dubai now.

exercises.explanationUz: Hozirgi xususiyat → ötmiş natija: would have + V3.
exercises.text: If he were more organised, he ___ ___ ___ (not / miss) the deadline last week.

exercises.explanationUz: Natija hozirga tegişli — would be.
exercises.question: Which sentence is correct?
options: If I had studied law, I would have been a lawyer now.
If I had studied law, I would be a lawyer now.
If I studied law, I would have been a lawyer now.
If I would study law, I would be a lawyer now.

exercises.explanationUz: Ötmiş şart + hozirgi natija.
exercises.source: Agar u keça yaxşi uxlaganida, hozir çarçagan bölmasdi.
accepted: If he had slept well last night, he wouldn’t be tired now
If he had slept well last night, he wouldn't be tired now
If she had slept well last night, she wouldn’t be tired now
If he had slept well last night, he would not be tired now
If she had slept well last night, she would not be tired now

exercises.explanationUz: If + had + V3, … would + fe’l + now.
identity — özlik, roots — ildizlar, erode — yemirmoq, hybrid — aralaş.

exercises.instructionUz: Grammatik qoida haqidagi fikr töğrimi (true) yoki xatomi (false)?
exercises.explanationUz: Aralaş şart gapda şart va natija turli vaqtga tegişli bölişi mumkin. Fikr töğri.
exercises.statement: In a mixed conditional, the condition and the result can refer to different times.

days.goalUz: Işlatiladi: hedging — appear / seem / tend to, may / might, It could be argued that, arguably, to some extent — diplomatik va xolis fikr bildiriş.

exercises.explanationUz: transparency — şaffoflik.
exercises.question: What does “transparency” mean?

exercises.explanationUz: seem to + fe’l.
exercises.question: The new policy ___ effective so far.

exercises.explanationUz: It could be argued that …
exercises.text: It could ___ ___ that the fine was too small.

exercises.instructionUz: Dalil kuçsiz bölganda eng mos fe’lni tanlang.
exercises.explanationUz: suggest — ehtiyotkor; prove — juda kuçli.
exercises.question: A single interview ___ that staff are unhappy.

exercises.explanationUz: “Ma’lum darajada” — to some extent.
exercises.source: Ma’lum darajada xaridorlar ham javobgar.
accepted: To some extent, customers are also responsible
To some extent customers are also responsible
To some extent, consumers are also responsible
Customers are also responsible to some extent

exercises.explanationUz: ega + tend + to + fe’l …
integrity — halollik, loophole — qonundagi böşliq, stakeholder — manfaatdor tomon, accountable — hisobdor.
Aniq faktlarga hedge kerak emas; uni haddan oşiriş matnni noaniq qiladi. Fikr xato.
exercises.statement: Good academic writing hedges every sentence, including clear facts.

days.goalUz: Işlatiladi: participle clauses — -ing, V3, having + V3, not + participle — ilmiy va rasmiy matnni ixçam yoziş.

exercises.explanationUz: replicate — takrorlab tasdiqlamoq.
exercises.question: What does “replicate” mean?

exercises.explanationUz: Passiv: The leaflet was printed → Printed.
exercises.question: ___ in large letters, the leaflet was easy to read.

exercises.explanationUz: Having + V3.
exercises.text: ___ ___ the experiment twice, they were sure of the result.

exercises.explanationUz: Inkor: Not + participle. Ega mos bölişi kerak.
exercises.question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: Not having enough water, the crops failed.
Having not enough water, the crops failed.
Not had enough water, the crops failed.
No having enough water, the crops failed.

exercises.explanationUz: “… da yaşab” — Living in …
exercises.source: Qişloqda yaşab, u fermerlarning muammolarini yaxşi tuşunardi.
accepted: Living in a village, he understood the farmers’ problems well
Living in a village, she understood the farmers’ problems well
Living in the village, he understood the farmers’ problems well
Living in the village, she understood the farmers’ problems well

exercises.explanationUz: V3 … , asosiy gap.
hypothesis — faraz, consensus — umumiy fikr, yield — hosil, funding — moliyalaştiriş.
“Walking to work, the bus was late” — xato: avtobus yurib ketmaydi, ega mos emas. Fikr töğri.
exercises.statement: In “Walking to work, the bus was late”, the participle does not match the subject.

days.goalUz: Işlatiladi: discourse markers (however, nevertheless, whereas, consequently) va nominalisation — izçil akademik esse yoziş.

exercises.explanationUz: coherent — izçil, mantiqli.
exercises.question: What does “coherent” mean?

exercises.explanationUz: Qöşimça dalil → Furthermore.
exercises.question: The scheme is cheap. ___, it is easy to manage.

exercises.explanationUz: introduce → introduction.
exercises.text: The ___ (introduce) of grants helped rural students.

exercises.explanationUz: “However” yangi gapni boşlaydi va undan keyin vergul qöyiladi. “Despite” dan keyin töliq gap emas, ot keladi; “However” bu yerda “although” örnini bosa olmaydi.
exercises.question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: The data were limited, despite the results were useful.
The data were limited. However, the results were useful.
The data were limited, nevertheless the results useful.
However the data were limited, the results were useful.

exercises.explanationUz: “Şunga qaramay” — Nevertheless.
exercises.source: Reja qimmat edi. Şunga qaramay, u tasdiqlandi.
accepted: The plan was expensive. Nevertheless, it was approved
The plan was expensive. Nevertheless it was approved
The plan was expensive. However, it was approved
The plan was expensive; nevertheless, it was approved

exercises.explanationUz: Gap, whereas gap.
draft — qoralama, cite — manbaga tayanmoq, plagiarism — plagiat, implication — oqibat.
Öz sözlaringiz bilan aytganda ham manbani körsatiş şart. Fikr xato.
exercises.statement: If you paraphrase an idea, you do not need to cite the source.

vocab.explanationEn: A set of reasons that someone uses to show that an idea is right or wrong.
vocab.exampleEn: Her argument was convincing because it was based on data.
vocab.exampleUz: Uning dalili işonarli edi, çunki ma’lumotlarga asoslangan edi.

vocab.explanationEn: Facts or information that show whether something is true.
vocab.exampleEn: There is little evidence that the diet works.
vocab.exampleUz: Bu parhez işlayotgani haqida dalil kam.

vocab.explanationEn: A tendency to support one side unfairly.
vocab.exampleEn: Every news source has some bias.
vocab.exampleUz: Har bir yangilik manbasida qandaydir tarafkaşlik bor.

vocab.explanationEn: Something you accept as true without proof.
vocab.exampleEn: The plan was based on the assumption that prices would fall.
vocab.exampleUz: Reja narxlar tuşadi degan taxminga asoslangan edi.

vocab.explanationEn: A false idea or a mistake in reasoning.
vocab.exampleEn: It is a fallacy that expensive things are always better.
vocab.exampleUz: Qimmat narsa doim yaxşiroq degan fikr — mantiqiy xato.

vocab.explanationEn: To make someone agree to do or believe something.
vocab.exampleEn: She persuaded the committee to change its decision.
vocab.exampleUz: U qömitani qarorini özgartirişga köndirdi.

vocab.explanationEn: A reason given against another argument.
vocab.exampleEn: A strong essay deals with the main counterarguments.
vocab.exampleUz: Kuçli esse asosiy qarşi dalillarni ham körib çiqadi.

vocab.explanationEn: A person, book or document that gives information.
vocab.exampleEn: Always check who wrote the source and when.
vocab.exampleUz: Manbani kim va qaçon yozganini doim tekşiring.

vocab.explanationEn: Not based on facts or evidence.
vocab.exampleEn: The rumours turned out to be completely unfounded.
vocab.exampleUz: Mişmişlar mutlaqo asossiz bölib çiqdi.

vocab.explanationEn: Speech or writing intended to persuade, sometimes without real content.
vocab.exampleEn: Behind the rhetoric, the plan contained few real ideas.
vocab.exampleUz: Baland sözlar ortida rejada haqiqiy ğoyalar kam edi.

vocab.explanationEn: To examine something very carefully.
vocab.exampleEn: Journalists scrutinised every number in the report.
vocab.exampleUz: Jurnalistlar hisobotdagi har bir raqamni sinçiklab tekşirişdi.

vocab.explanationEn: Giving a wrong idea or impression.
vocab.exampleEn: The headline was technically true but misleading.
vocab.exampleUz: Sarlavha texnik jihatdan töğri, lekin çalğituvçi edi.

vocab.explanationEn: The supply of workers and the jobs available in an economy.
vocab.exampleEn: The labour market for engineers is very competitive.
vocab.exampleUz: Muhandislar uçun mehnat bozori juda raqobatli.

vocab.explanationEn: The situation in which people who want to work cannot find a job.
vocab.exampleEn: Youth unemployment is a concern in many regions.
vocab.exampleUz: Köp hududlarda yoşlar işsizligi xavotirga sabab bölmoqda.

vocab.explanationEn: The difference between the skills employers need and the skills workers have.
vocab.exampleEn: Companies blame the skills gap for unfilled vacancies.
vocab.exampleUz: Kompaniyalar böş örinlar uçun könikmalar yetişmovçiligini ayblaydi.

vocab.explanationEn: A person or organisation that pays people to work for them.
vocab.exampleEn: Employers increasingly value practical experience.
vocab.exampleUz: Iş beruvçilar amaliy tajribani tobora köproq qadrlamoqda.

vocab.explanationEn: A job that is available for someone to do.
vocab.exampleEn: There are three vacancies in the accounts department.
vocab.exampleUz: Buxgalteriya bölimida uçta böş iş örni bor.

vocab.explanationEn: An official record showing that you have finished a course or have skills.
vocab.exampleEn: A degree is no longer enough; employers look for other qualifications too.
vocab.exampleUz: Diplom endi yetarli emas; iş beruvçilar boşqa malakalarni ham izlaydi.

vocab.explanationEn: A situation in which two things do not fit together.
vocab.exampleEn: There is a mismatch between what universities teach and what businesses need.
vocab.exampleUz: Universitetlar örgatayotgan narsa va biznes ehtiyoji örtasida nomuvofiqlik bor.

vocab.explanationEn: A person who moves to another place or country to find work.
vocab.exampleEn: Many labour migrants send money home to their families.
vocab.exampleUz: Köp mehnat muhojirlari oilalariga pul jönatadi.

vocab.explanationEn: Money sent home by people working abroad.
vocab.exampleEn: Remittances help many households pay for education.
vocab.exampleUz: Pul ötkazmalari köp oilalarga ta’lim xarajatlarini qoplaşga yordam beradi.

vocab.explanationEn: A person who starts their own business, often taking risks.
vocab.exampleEn: Young entrepreneurs need cheaper loans.
vocab.exampleUz: Yoş tadbirkorlarga arzonroq kreditlar kerak.

vocab.explanationEn: Something that encourages a person to do something.
vocab.exampleEn: Tax incentives encouraged firms to hire graduates.
vocab.exampleUz: Soliq imtiyozlari firmalarni bitiruvçilarni işga olişga rağbatlantirdi.

vocab.explanationEn: Having more education or experience than a job needs.
vocab.exampleEn: She was rejected because she was overqualified.
vocab.exampleUz: Malakasi lavozimdan yuqori bölgani uçun uni qabul qilişmadi.

vocab.explanationEn: A route used by merchants to carry goods between places.
vocab.exampleEn: Samarkand grew rich because it lay on a major trade route.
vocab.exampleUz: Samarqand yirik savdo yölida joylaşgani uçun boyib ketgan.

vocab.explanationEn: A person who buys and sells goods, especially in large amounts.
vocab.exampleEn: Merchants carried silk, spices and paper across the desert.
vocab.exampleUz: Savdogarlar çöl orqali ipak, ziravorlar va qoğoz olib ötişgan.

vocab.explanationEn: The series of steps involved in producing and delivering a product.
vocab.exampleEn: The pandemic disrupted global supply chains.
vocab.exampleUz: Pandemiya global ta’minot zanjirlarini izdan çiqardi.

vocab.explanationEn: A tax on goods coming into or going out of a country.
vocab.exampleEn: Higher tariffs made imported cars more expensive.
vocab.exampleUz: Yuqori bojlar import maşinalarni qimmatlaştirdi.

vocab.explanationEn: To sell goods to another country.
vocab.exampleEn: Uzbekistan exports fruit and textiles to many countries.
vocab.exampleUz: Özbekiston köp mamlakatlarga meva va töqimaçilik mahsulotlari eksport qiladi.

vocab.explanationEn: A general increase in prices and fall in the value of money.
vocab.exampleEn: Inflation means that your salary buys less each year.
vocab.exampleUz: Inflyatsiya maoşingiz har yili kamroq narsaga yetişini anglatadi.

vocab.explanationEn: To stop something from continuing normally.
vocab.exampleEn: The storm disrupted deliveries for a week.
vocab.exampleUz: Böron bir hafta davomida yetkazib berişni izdan çiqardi.

vocab.explanationEn: Depending on each other.
vocab.exampleEn: Modern economies are highly interdependent.
vocab.exampleUz: Zamonaviy iqtisodiyotlar özaro juda boğliq.

vocab.explanationEn: To bring something back into use or popularity.
vocab.exampleEn: New railways may revive the old trade routes.
vocab.exampleUz: Yangi temir yöllar eski savdo yöllarini qayta jonlantirişi mumkin.

vocab.explanationEn: A raw material or product that can be bought and sold, such as cotton or gold.
vocab.exampleEn: Gold and cotton are important commodities.
vocab.exampleUz: Oltin va paxta — muhim xomaşyo tovarlari.

vocab.explanationEn: Surrounded by land, with no coast.
vocab.exampleEn: Uzbekistan is one of only two doubly landlocked countries in the world.
vocab.exampleUz: Özbekiston dunyodagi ikki karra dengizga çiqişi yöq ikki mamlakatdan biri.

vocab.explanationEn: The organisation of moving and storing goods.
vocab.exampleEn: Good logistics can cut delivery times in half.
vocab.exampleUz: Yaxşi logistika yetkazib beriş vaqtini ikki baravar qisqartirişi mumkin.

vocab.explanationEn: Who a person is; the qualities and beliefs that make them different from others.
vocab.exampleEn: Language is a central part of our identity.
vocab.exampleUz: Til — özligimizning markaziy qismi.

vocab.explanationEn: People who live outside the country their families came from.
vocab.exampleEn: The Uzbek diaspora in Turkey is growing.
vocab.exampleUz: Turkiyadagi özbek diasporasi kattalaşmoqda.

vocab.explanationEn: Able to speak two languages equally well.
vocab.exampleEn: Their children are bilingual in Uzbek and Russian.
vocab.exampleUz: Ularning farzandlari özbek va rus tillarida birdek gaplaşadi.

vocab.explanationEn: To become part of a new country or culture.
vocab.exampleEn: Some immigrants assimilate quickly; others keep their traditions.
vocab.exampleUz: Ayrim muhojirlar tez singib ketadi, boşqalari an’analarini saqlaydi.

vocab.explanationEn: A language spoken by your family but not by the wider society where you live.
vocab.exampleEn: Weekend schools help children keep their heritage language.
vocab.exampleUz: Dam oliş kunlari maktablari bolalarga ota-bobolar tilini saqlaşga yordam beradi.

vocab.explanationEn: The feeling of being accepted as part of a group.
vocab.exampleEn: Sport can give young migrants a sense of belonging.
vocab.exampleUz: Sport yoş muhojirlarga mansublik hissini berişi mumkin.

vocab.explanationEn: To make someone leave the place where they have lived for a long time.
vocab.exampleEn: The war uprooted thousands of families.
vocab.exampleUz: Uruş minglab oilalarni tub joyidan ayirdi.

vocab.explanationEn: Consisting of parts or people that are all the same.
vocab.exampleEn: Global brands are making cities look more homogeneous.
vocab.exampleUz: Global brendlar şaharlarni bir xil körinişga keltirmoqda.

vocab.explanationEn: To accept new ideas or changes willingly.
vocab.exampleEn: Young people embrace foreign music without forgetting their own.
vocab.exampleUz: Yoşlar öz musiqasini unutmay, xorijiy musiqani qabul qiladi.

vocab.explanationEn: The place or culture that a person or their family comes from.
vocab.exampleEn: She visited Bukhara to discover her roots.
vocab.exampleUz: U öz ildizlarini kaşf qiliş uçun Buxoroga bordi.

vocab.explanationEn: To gradually destroy something.
vocab.exampleEn: Some fear that globalisation will erode local traditions.
vocab.exampleUz: Ayrimlar globallaşuv mahalliy an’analarni asta-sekin yemiradi, deb qörqadi.

vocab.explanationEn: A mixture of two or more different things.
vocab.exampleEn: Many young people have a hybrid identity.
vocab.exampleUz: Köp yoşlarda aralaş özlik bor.

vocab.explanationEn: Moral principles that control how people behave.
vocab.exampleEn: Business ethics are taught in every MBA programme.
vocab.exampleUz: Biznes etikasi har bir MBA dasturida örgatiladi.

vocab.explanationEn: Being open and honest about decisions and information.
vocab.exampleEn: Investors demand more transparency about salaries.
vocab.exampleUz: Investorlar maoşlar haqida köproq şaffoflik talab qilmoqda.

vocab.explanationEn: Responsible for your decisions and expected to explain them.
vocab.exampleEn: Managers must be held accountable for safety failures.
vocab.exampleUz: Rahbarlar xavfsizlik bilan boğliq xatolar uçun javob berişi kerak.

vocab.explanationEn: To treat someone unfairly in order to gain an advantage.
vocab.exampleEn: Some suppliers were found to exploit child workers.
vocab.exampleUz: Ayrim yetkazib beruvçilar bolalar mehnatidan nohaq foydalangani aniqlandi.

vocab.explanationEn: The quality of being honest and having strong moral principles.
vocab.exampleEn: She is known for her integrity.
vocab.exampleUz: U halolligi bilan tanilgan.

vocab.explanationEn: A person who tells the public about illegal or wrong activity in an organisation.
vocab.exampleEn: The whistleblower lost her job but saved many lives.
vocab.exampleUz: Xabar bergan xodim işini yöqotdi, lekin köp hayotni saqlab qoldi.

vocab.explanationEn: Making a company seem more environmentally friendly than it really is.
vocab.exampleEn: Calling plastic bottles “eco” is a clear case of greenwashing.
vocab.exampleUz: Plastik idişni “eko” deb ataş — soxta yaşil reklamaning yaqqol namunasi.

vocab.explanationEn: A person or group affected by a business, such as workers, customers or neighbours.
vocab.exampleEn: Local residents are important stakeholders in the mining project.
vocab.exampleUz: Mahalliy aholi kon loyihasidagi muhim manfaatdor tomon hisoblanadi.

vocab.explanationEn: Used when giving an opinion that you think could be supported.
vocab.exampleEn: This is arguably the most important decision of the year.
vocab.exampleUz: Aytiş mumkinki, bu yilning eng muhim qarori.

vocab.explanationEn: To usually behave in a particular way.
vocab.exampleEn: Customers tend to trust brands that admit their mistakes.
vocab.exampleUz: Xaridorlar xatosini tan oladigan brendlarga köproq işonişga moyil.

vocab.explanationEn: A small mistake in a law that allows people to avoid obeying it.
vocab.exampleEn: The company used a legal loophole to avoid paying tax.
vocab.exampleUz: Kompaniya soliq tölamaslik uçun qonundagi böşliqdan foydalandi.

vocab.explanationEn: The opinion that people have about someone or something.
vocab.exampleEn: One scandal can destroy a company’s reputation.
vocab.exampleUz: Bitta janjal kompaniya obröyini yöq qilişi mumkin.

vocab.explanationEn: An important discovery or development.

grammar.titleEn: Inversion after negative and limiting adverbials
explanationUz: Inversion — gap boşida inkor yoki çeklovçi ibora kelganda yordamçi fe’l egadan OLDIN keladi (söroq gapdagidek): Never have I seen such a clear argument. Bu rasmiy, ta’kidli uslub — notiqlik, esse va maqolalarda köp uçraydi, oddiy suhbatda kam.

Asosiy iboralar: never, rarely, seldom, hardly ever, at no time, under no circumstances, not only … but also, not until, only then / only after / only when, little. Rarely do we question the sources we trust. Not only did the report ignore the data, but it also misquoted experts.

Vaqt ketma-ketligi: No sooner had … than … va Hardly / Scarcely had … when … — “… bilanoq” ma’nosida: No sooner had the minister finished his speech than the journalists started asking questions. Bu yerda Past Perfect keladi.

Only + vaqt / şart bölagi bölsa, inversion ASOSIY gapda böladi: Only when we checked the original study did we notice the error. Agar yordamçi fe’l bölmasa, do / does / did qöşiladi: Little did they know that the data was false.

formula.noteUz: Not only is the claim unfounded, but it is also dangerous.

formula.form: No sooner had + ega + V3 + than …
formula.noteUz: No sooner had the article appeared than it was shared thousands of times.

formula.form: Only when / after … + yordamçi + ega + fe’l

explanationUz: Cleft (“ikkiga bölingan”) gap — bitta qismni ta’kidlaş uçun gapni ikki bölakka ajratiş. It-cleft: It + be + ta’kidlanayotgan qism + that / who … Oddiy gap: The skills gap worries employers. Ta’kid: It is the skills gap that worries employers (aynan könikmalar yetişmovçiligi).

Wh-cleft (pseudo-cleft): What + ega + fe’l + be + ta’kidlanayotgan qism. What employers want is practical experience. Harakatni ta’kidlaş uçun do bilan: What the government did was (to) reduce taxes for small businesses.

Boşqa şakllar: All (that) … is …: All I want is a fair salary (faqat şuni xohlayman). The reason (why) … is that …: The reason why graduates leave is that wages are low. The thing that … is …, The place where … is …

Nutq va yozuvda cleft gaplar qarşi fikrni töğrilaş uçun foydali: It wasn’t the lack of jobs that caused the problem — it was the lack of information about them. Zamon be fe’lida ifodalanadi: It was in 2017 that the reform began.

grammar.titleUz: Impersonal passive: It is said that … / X is said to …
explanationUz: Ilmiy, rasmiy va yangilik matnlarida fikrning manbasini ta’kidlamaslik uçun impersonal passive işlatiladi. Birinçi usul: It + is / was + V3 (said, believed, thought, reported, estimated, expected, claimed) + that … — It is believed that the city was founded in the 6th century BC.

Ikkinçi usul: ega + is / was + V3 + to + fe’l. Harakat bir vaqtda bölsa — to + boşlanğiç fe’l: The company is said to employ 2,000 people. Harakat OLDIN bölgan bölsa — to have + V3: Samarkand is believed to have been founded more than 2,500 years ago.

Davom etayotgan iş uçun — to be + V-ing: Prices are expected to be rising next year. Mavjudlik uçun There dan foydalaniladi: There are thought to be thousands of unregistered workers. Bu tuzilmalar xabar beruvçini “men eşitdim” deb emas, umumiy fikr sifatida körsatadi.
Ehtiyot böling: muallif fikrini bu tuzilma orqali “yaşirib” yuboriş ham mumkin. Tanqidiy öquvçi doim sörasin: kim aytgan? qanday dalil bor? “It is said that …” — da’vo, isbot emas.

explanationUz: Aralaş şart gaplarda şart va natija turli vaqtga tegişli böladi. Eng köp uçraydigan tur: ÖTMIŞDAGI xayoliy şart → HOZIRGI natija. If + had + V3, … would + fe’l: If my parents hadn’t moved to Istanbul, I would speak Uzbek better now.

Ikkinçi tur: HOZIRGI (doimiy) xayoliy holat → ÖTMIŞDAGI natija. If + Past Simple, … would have + V3: If I weren’t so shy, I would have asked her for her phone number at the party. Bu yerda şart hozir ham töğri bölgan xususiyat (uyatçanlik).

Natijada could, might ham keladi: If she had studied Chinese at school, she could be working in Shanghai now. Agar ikkalasi ham ötmişga tegişli bölsa — oddiy Third Conditional; ikkalasi ham hozirga — Second Conditional. Aralaş tur vaqt ifodalari bilan aniq körinadi: now, today, at the moment, yesterday, last year.

Inkor va savollar: If he hadn’t lost his passport, he wouldn’t be stuck at the airport now. What would you be doing now if you hadn’t chosen this university? Rasmiy uslubda if’siz inversion ham mumkin: Had I known, I would be there now.

explanationUz: Discourse markers — fikrlar orasidagi mantiqiy boğlanişni körsatuvçi sözlar. Qöşiş: furthermore, moreover, in addition. Qarama-qarşilik: however, nevertheless, whereas, on the other hand. Natija: therefore, consequently, as a result. Misol: for instance, such as. Xulosa: in conclusion, overall.

Gapdagi örni muhim. However, nevertheless, consequently, furthermore — odatda yangi gap boşida, keyin vergul: Prices rose. However, sales did not fall. Whereas va although — bitta gap ichida ikki qismni boğlaydi: Prices rose, whereas sales stayed the same. “However” bilan ikki gapni faqat vergul bilan ulab bölmaydi — nuqta yoki nuqtali vergul kerak.

Nominalisation — fe’l yoki sifatni otga aylantiriş: decide → decision, grow → growth, fail → failure, important → importance. Akademik matnda fikr ixçam va obyektiv böladi: Because prices increased, people bought less → The increase in prices led to a fall in demand.

Me’yorni saqlang: har bir gapni ot zanjiriga aylantiriş matnni oğir qiladi. Yaxşi akademik uslub — aniq fe’llar va örinli nominalisation aralaşmasi. Bitta abzasda bir xil markerni qayta-qayta işlatmang.

reading.title: Why Smart People Believe False Headlines
paragraphs: It is tempting to assume that only careless or poorly educated people fall for misleading news. Yet research in psychology suggests otherwise. Intelligence, it turns out, offers surprisingly little protection against misinformation; in some cases it may even make people better at defending what they already believe. Psychologists call this “motivated reasoning”: rather than following the evidence wherever it leads, we use our reasoning skills to reach the conclusion we wanted in the first place.

Consider a typical example. A dramatic headline claims that a common food causes a serious illness. Readers who already distrust the food industry share it within seconds. Only later, if at all, do they discover that the study involved a handful of mice and that the headline exaggerated its findings. Not only does the false version travel faster than the correction, but it also tends to be remembered longer, because it is simpler and more emotional.

What, then, can be done? Teachers increasingly focus on habits rather than knowledge. Before sharing a claim, students are encouraged to ask three questions: Who is behind this information? What is the evidence? What do other sources say? Under no circumstances, they are told, should a single screenshot be treated as proof. Such habits sound modest, but they work best precisely because they slow us down at the moment when our emotions are pushing us to react.

reading.title: Diplomas Without Jobs, Jobs Without Workers
paragraphs: Every summer, thousands of graduates leave universities across Central Asia full of hope, and every autumn many of them discover the same uncomfortable truth: a diploma is not a job. At the same time, employers complain that they cannot find qualified staff. Economists call this paradox a skills mismatch, and what makes it so frustrating is that both sides are, in a sense, right.

It is not simply that there are too few jobs. In fields such as welding, nursing and software testing, vacancies often stay open for months. What many graduates lack is not knowledge but practical experience: they have studied theory for four years without spending a single week in a real workplace. Some solutions are already being tested. A number of companies now run paid apprenticeships in partnership with local colleges, and several universities have made internships a compulsory part of their degree programmes. What these approaches have in common is that they bring education and work closer together. The reason why change is slow, critics argue, is that prestige still matters more to families than practical prospects. Until attitudes shift, many talented young people will continue to look for opportunities abroad.

reading.title: The New Silk Road: Promise and Doubt
paragraphs: For more than a thousand years, caravans crossed Central Asia carrying silk, spices, paper and ideas between East and West. Cities such as Samarkand and Bukhara are believed to have owed much of their wealth to this trade. When sea routes became cheaper in the sixteenth century, however, the overland routes lost much of their importance, and the region was gradually pushed to the edge of global commerce.

Today there is talk of a revival. New railways, highways and logistics centres are being built, and it is widely claimed that goods could travel from eastern China to Europe by land in less than half the time a ship needs. For a landlocked country like Uzbekistan, which has to cross at least two borders to reach any sea, faster land routes are thought to offer a real chance to expand exports of fruit, textiles and manufactured goods.

Not everyone is convinced. Critics point out that rail freight is still considerably more expensive than sea freight for most goods, and that the benefits are said to go mainly to large companies rather than to local producers. There are also thought to be risks of rising debt where infrastructure is financed by foreign loans. What is clear is that roads and railways alone will not revive the old prosperity; the region will also need efficient customs, reliable rules and skilled workers who can take advantage of them.

reading.title: Between Two Languages
paragraphs: Lola Rahmatova was born in Moscow to parents who had moved there from Samarkand in the 1990s. At home they spoke a mixture of Uzbek and Russian; at school, only Russian. By the time she was a teenager, she understood her grandmother perfectly but answered her in Russian. “If my parents had insisted on Uzbek at home,” she says now, “I would probably be fluent today. But they were working long hours, and Russian was simply easier.”

Her story is typical of many children in diaspora families. Linguists describe a familiar pattern: the first generation keeps its language, the second generation understands it but prefers the majority language, and by the third generation it has often disappeared. What is lost is not only vocabulary but a whole way of seeing the world — jokes, proverbs, songs, and the ability to talk with older relatives about the past.

Lola decided to break the pattern. At twenty-six she spent a year in Samarkand, attending classes in the morning and helping in her uncle’s shop in the afternoon. Today she runs an online club where young people from the diaspora practise Uzbek together. She admits that her identity is a hybrid one. “If I had grown up in Uzbekistan, I wouldn’t understand Moscow the way I do,” she says. “I don’t think I have to choose. Both languages are mine — I just had to work harder for one of them.”

reading.title: Is “Green” Always Green?
paragraphs: In recent years, supermarket shelves across the world have filled with products labelled “eco”, “natural” or “planet-friendly”. Surveys in many countries suggest that a growing number of shoppers are willing to pay more for goods they believe are better for the environment. It is hardly surprising, then, that companies have rushed to present themselves as green. What is less clear is how many of these claims would survive close scrutiny.

Critics use the term “greenwashing” to describe marketing that exaggerates a product’s environmental benefits. A bottle made with a small percentage of recycled plastic may be advertised as if it had no impact at all; a fashion brand may promote one “sustainable” collection while the rest of its production remains unchanged. Such practices are not always illegal, but they arguably undermine the trust on which genuine efforts depend.

Some regulators have begun to respond. In several markets, companies are now required to support environmental claims with evidence, and vague words such as “eco-friendly” are discouraged unless they are clearly explained. Responsible firms, for their part, tend to be more specific: rather than calling a product “green”, they state exactly what has changed and by how much. For consumers, the lesson would seem to be a simple one. The more general and emotional a claim is, the more questions it probably deserves.

reading.title: From the Lab to the Field
paragraphs: Scientific breakthroughs are often imagined as dramatic moments in a laboratory. In reality, much of the hardest work begins after the discovery, when researchers try to persuade people to use what they have found. A drought-resistant variety of wheat, for example, is of little value if it remains in a seed bank. Having spent years developing such varieties, scientists frequently discover that the greatest obstacle is not biology but trust.

Farmers have good reasons to be sceptical. Faced with uncertain weather and tight budgets, they cannot afford to experiment with a crop that might fail. Promises made by outsiders have sometimes proved unreliable in the past. For this reason, many agricultural researchers now prefer to work alongside farmers from the start, planting trial plots on ordinary farms rather than on protected research stations. Seeing the results in a neighbour’s field tends to be far more convincing than reading a report.

Communication matters too. Written in technical language, a research paper may be perfectly accurate and still useless to the people who need it most. Successful outreach programmes translate findings into local languages, use photographs and simple measurements, and invite questions rather than demanding acceptance. Not every project succeeds, but those built on genuine dialogue appear to last longer. Science, it seems, does not end with publication; in many ways it only begins there.

reading.title: Writing to Be Understood
paragraphs: Many students arrive at university believing that academic writing should sound difficult. Long words, complex sentences and impersonal phrases, they assume, are signs of intelligence. Experienced writers tend to disagree. In their view, the purpose of an essay is not to impress the reader but to guide them, step by step, towards a clear conclusion. A coherent argument is one that a reader can follow without having to read any sentence twice.

Discourse markers play a central role in this process. Words such as however, consequently and for instance work like road signs, telling the reader whether the next idea adds to, contrasts with or results from the previous one. Used well, they make the structure of an argument visible. Used carelessly, however, they can confuse: a paragraph in which every sentence begins with “Moreover” suggests a list rather than a line of reasoning.

Nominalisation raises a similar issue. Turning verbs into nouns allows writers to pack information into fewer words and to sound more objective: “The introduction of tuition fees” is more concise than “When the government introduced tuition fees”. Nevertheless, an essay built entirely from abstract nouns can become heavy and unclear. The best academic writing, it seems, combines both strategies, using nouns to summarise ideas and active verbs to show who did what.

writing.promptEn: “Schools should teach critical thinking as a separate subject.” Write an argumentative essay. Present arguments on both sides, deal with the strongest counterargument and give a reasoned conclusion.
writing.instructionUz: “Maktablarda tanqidiy fikrlaş alohida fan sifatida örgatilişi kerak” mavzusida argumentativ esse yozing: ikkala tomon dalillari, eng kuçli qarşi dalilga javob va asoslangan xulosa. Kamida ikkita inversion (Not only …, Rarely …, Only when …) işlating.
checklistUz: Kirişda muammo va tezis (öz pozitsiyangiz) aniq.
Har paragrafda bitta asosiy fikr va dalil.
Eng kuçli qarşi dalil adolatli bayon qilingan va javob berilgan.
Kamida ikkita inversion ta’kid uçun işlatilgan.
Xulosa yangi fikr kiritmasdan tezisni mustahkamlaydi.
writing.modelAnswerEn: In an age when a single viral post can shape public opinion overnight, the ability to evaluate information has become as basic as literacy itself. Supporters of a separate subject argue that critical thinking is too important to be left to chance. Not only would a dedicated course give the skill a clear place in the timetable, but it would also allow teachers to be properly trained. Rarely, they point out, is a skill mastered when it is everybody’s responsibility and nobody’s priority. The strongest counterargument, however, is that thinking cannot be separated from content. Critics claim that students learn to question evidence best when they analyse a real historical source or a flawed scientific experiment, not when they memorise lists of logical fallacies. There is considerable evidence for this view: transfer of abstract skills to new situations is notoriously weak. Yet this objection does not rule out a separate subject; it shapes how it should be taught. A course built around real cases from history, science and the media could combine both approaches. In conclusion, critical thinking deserves its own place in the curriculum, provided that it is taught through meaningful content rather than as an abstract set of rules.

writing.promptEn: Your regional youth council has asked for proposals to reduce youth unemployment. Write a proposal describing the main causes of the problem in your area and recommending two practical measures.
writing.instructionUz: Hududiy yoşlar kengaşi yoşlar işsizligini kamaytiriş böyicha takliflar sörayapti. Taklifnoma yozing: hududingizdagi muammoning asosiy sabablari va ikkita amaliy çora. Kamida uçta cleft gap (What … is …, It is … that …, The reason why … is that …) işlating.
checklistUz: Sarlavha va bölim nomlari (Introduction, Causes, Recommendations, Conclusion).
Rasmiy, xolis uslub; soxta statistika yöq.
Kamida uçta cleft gap ta’kid uçun işlatilgan.
Har bir taklif aniq va amalga oşirib bölinadigan.
Kutilayotgan natija xulosada.

mustInclude.whyUz: Wh-cleft gap: “What young people need is …”.

writing.modelAnswerEn: Proposal: Reducing Youth Unemployment in Our District. Introduction. This proposal outlines the main causes of youth unemployment in our district and recommends two measures that could be introduced within a year. Causes. It is not a shortage of jobs alone that keeps young people out of work. Local construction firms and clinics regularly report unfilled vacancies. What many school leavers lack is practical experience and information about these opportunities. The reason why vocational courses remain unpopular is that families often see them as a second-class choice. Recommendations. Firstly, I recommend a paid summer placement scheme, run jointly by the council and local employers, so that students in their final two years can spend six weeks in a real workplace. Secondly, the council should organise an annual careers fair in the district centre, where employers, colleges and successful former students explain what different jobs actually involve. Conclusion. What these measures have in common is that they connect young people directly with employers. If introduced, they would make the local labour market more transparent and give young people a realistic alternative to looking for work abroad.

Faktlar va taxminlar farqlangan; soxta raqamlar yöq.
Kamida törtta impersonal passive tuzilma.
Har bir imkoniyat / xavfga aniq misol.
Xulosada tavsiya.

Ötmişga oid taxmin: “… is thought to have …”.

writing.modelAnswerEn: Report: Trade and the Future of the Zarafshan Valley. Introduction. This report considers how increased regional trade might affect the Zarafshan Valley, an area historically linked to the Silk Road. Opportunities. The valley is believed to have some of the best conditions in the country for growing apricots and grapes, and new cold-storage centres are expected to reduce the share of fruit that is currently lost before reaching buyers. It is widely thought that improved rail links to neighbouring countries will make it easier for small farmers to sell abroad. Tourism is also said to be benefiting from easier travel, which creates jobs for guides, drivers and guesthouse owners. Risks. However, it is not yet clear who will gain most from these changes. Large exporters are reported to have received most of the new contracts, while small producers often lack the information and certificates needed to compete. There are also thought to be environmental risks if water use grows faster than supply. Conclusion. Greater trade offers real potential, but it is recommended that local authorities provide training and advice for small producers, so that the benefits are shared more widely.

Har paragrafda bitta asosiy fikr va aniq misol.
Qarşi fikr adolatli körib çiqilgan.
Kamida ikkita aralaş şart gap.
Xulosa nyuansli (oq-qora emas).

Savol “to what extent” — javobda ham daraja körsatilsin.

writing.modelAnswerEn: Walk through any large city today and you will see the same coffee chains, the same films and the same fashions. It is therefore understandable that many people fear globalisation is erasing local cultures. I agree with this view only to a limited extent. On the one hand, some losses are real. Small crafts that once supported whole villages cannot compete with cheap factory goods, and many young people know more about foreign celebrities than about their own poets. If craft schools had received more support twenty years ago, more young artisans would be working in places like Rishtan and Margilan today. On the other hand, globalisation has also given local cultures new audiences. Uzbek musicians now reach listeners abroad through streaming platforms, and online shops allow embroiderers to sell directly to customers in Europe. If these tools did not exist, many of those artists would never have found buyers outside their own region. In conclusion, globalisation is not simply destroying local cultures; it is changing the conditions in which they survive. Cultures that are actively taught, valued and shared are more likely to adapt than to disappear.

writing.modelAnswerEn: Dear Ms Sultanova, I am writing about the posts that have appeared on social media this week claiming that our “Green Line” packaging is misleading. At this stage, it would appear that the criticism is partly justified. Our labels describe the bottles as “eco-friendly”, but only around a third of the plastic is recycled, and this is not clearly stated. On the other hand, some of the claims online seem to be exaggerated; there is no evidence that our factory has increased its emissions. I would recommend three steps. First, we should acknowledge the problem quickly. Customers tend to be more forgiving when a company responds openly rather than defensively. Second, the vague term “eco-friendly” should be replaced by a precise statement of the recycled content. Third, it might be worth inviting an independent expert to review our other environmental claims before they are questioned too. Arguably, the cost of these changes is small compared with the damage that a long online campaign could do to our reputation. I would be happy to prepare a draft statement if that would be helpful. Kind regards, Jasur Ergashev

writing.modelAnswerEn: Report: Sharing information about drip irrigation. Introduction. The aim of this report is to recommend how the council can explain the new drip irrigation method to local farmers. Having spoken to twelve farmers in three villages, I have identified the main concerns. Findings. Most farmers have heard of drip irrigation but are unsure about the cost. Worried about losing a harvest, they are unlikely to change their methods on the basis of a leaflet alone. Information written in technical terms was described as “hard to follow” by almost everyone I interviewed. Recommendations. First, I recommend setting up two demonstration fields on ordinary farms, managed by respected local farmers. Seeing the results with their own eyes, neighbours are far more likely to trust the method. Second, any printed material should be short, written in Uzbek and Karakalpak, and illustrated with photographs. Third, an agronomist should visit each village at least twice during the season, answering questions in person. Conclusion. Supported by practical examples and clear language, the new method has a good chance of being widely adopted within two or three years.

writing.promptEn: “University education should be free for all students.” To what extent do you agree? Write an academic essay with a clear thesis, two main arguments, one counterargument and a conclusion.
writing.instructionUz: “Oliy ta’lim barça talabalar uçun bepul bölişi kerak.” Qay darajada qöşilasiz? Akademik esse yozing: aniq tezis, ikki asosiy dalil, bitta qarşi dalil va xulosa. Discourse markers va nominalisation’dan örinli foydalaning.
checklistUz: Kirişning oxirida aniq tezis.
Har paragraf bitta asosiy fikr atrofida.
Turli discourse markers (bir xilini takrorlamaslik).
Kamida bitta qarşi dalil va unga javob.
Xulosada yangi dalil emas, tezisni mustahkamlaş.
writing.modelAnswerEn: Free higher education is often presented as a simple question of fairness. In my view, however, a system in which fees depend on family income would be both fairer and more sustainable than one in which university is free for everyone. The first argument concerns fairness. When university is free, taxpayers on low incomes help to pay for the education of students from wealthy families, who could easily afford the fees. An income-based system, by contrast, directs public money to those who need it most. Furthermore, the introduction of grants for low-income students has, in several countries, increased the number of applicants from rural areas. The second argument relates to quality. Universities require stable funding for libraries, laboratories and qualified staff. Where tuition is free, governments often struggle to meet these costs; consequently, class sizes grow and standards may fall. Supporters of free education argue that any fee discourages talented but poor students. This concern is serious. Nevertheless, it is an argument against badly designed fees rather than against fees in general: a well-designed scheme charges nothing to families below a certain income, whereas wealthier families pay a fair share. In conclusion, the goal of equal access is better achieved through targeted support than through free tuition for all. The real question is not whether students should pay, but who should pay and how much.

speaking.questionEn: Report a recent piece of economic news you heard, using cautious language where the facts are uncertain.
speaking.hintUz: “It has been reported that …”, “… is expected to …”, “… is said to have …” tuzilmalari.
speaking.textAlternative: Yaqinda eşitgan iqtisodiy yangilikni ehtiyotkor til bilan 7 gapda yozing.
followUpsEn: Where did you hear it?
How reliable is the source?

speaking.questionEn: How would your life be different now if you had been born in another country?
speaking.hintUz: Aralaş şart gaplar bilan gapiring: “If I had been born in …, I would … now”.
speaking.textAlternative: Boşqa mamlakatda tuğilganingizda hayotingiz hozir qanday bölişi haqida 8–10 gap yozing.
followUpsEn: Which language would you speak at home?
What would you miss most?

speaking.questionEn: To what extent is language a part of a person’s identity?
speaking.hintUz: Şaxsiy tajriba va boşqalar misolini keltiring; nyuansli javob bering.
speaking.textAlternative: Til va özlik örtasidagi boğliqlik haqida 8–10 gap yozing.
followUpsEn: Can someone have two identities?
Should parents abroad insist on their language?

speaking.questionEn: Describe a decision in your past that still affects your life today.
speaking.hintUz: “If I hadn’t …, I wouldn’t be … now” tuzilmasini kamida bir marta işlating.
speaking.textAlternative: Hozirgi hayotingizga ta’sir qilgan ötmişdagi qaror haqida 8 gap yozing.
followUpsEn: Do you regret it?
Who influenced that decision?

speaking.questionEn: Your manager asks you to hide a small product defect from customers to meet sales targets. What would you do?
speaking.hintUz: Variantlarni tarozida tortib körsating, ehtiyotkor til işlating: “It could be argued that …”, “I would probably …”.
speaking.textAlternative: Mahsulot nuqsonini yaşiriş haqidagi dilemmada qanday yöl tutişingizni 8–10 gapda yozing.
followUpsEn: What might the consequences be?
Who else would you talk to?

speaking.questionEn: What makes you trust or distrust a company?
speaking.hintUz: Aniq misollar keltiring va umumlaştirişlarni yumşating: “Companies tend to …”.
speaking.textAlternative: Kompaniyalarga işonç yoki işonçsizlik sabablari haqida 8 gap yozing.
followUpsEn: Have you ever stopped buying a brand?
Do reviews influence you?

speaking.questionEn: Can a company be both very profitable and completely ethical?
speaking.hintUz: Ikki tomonni körib çiqing, keskin xulosadan qoçing: “To some extent …”.
speaking.textAlternative: Kompaniya bir vaqtda foydali va axloqiy böla oladimi — 8–10 gap yozing.
followUpsEn: Can you name an example?
Who should set the rules?

speaking.questionEn: Why do some people distrust scientific advice, and what could change that?
speaking.hintUz: Sabablarni tahlil qiling va 1–2 ta participle clause qöşing: “Having seen …, people …”.
speaking.textAlternative: Odamlar nega ilmiy maslahatga işonmasligi haqida 8–10 gap yozing.
followUpsEn: Who do you trust for health advice?
What role does social media play?

speaking.questionEn: Describe a scientific discovery that has changed life in your family or region.
speaking.hintUz: Oldin va keyin taqqoslang: “Introduced in the 1990s, … changed …”.
speaking.textAlternative: Oilangiz yoki viloyatingiz hayotini özgartirgan kaşfiyot haqida 8 gap yozing.
followUpsEn: Were there any disadvantages?
What will the next big change be?

speaking.questionEn: Should governments fund research that has no obvious practical use?
speaking.hintUz: Ikki tomonning dalillarini keltiring, misol bilan asoslang.
speaking.textAlternative: Amaliy foydasi aniq bölmagan tadqiqotlarni davlat moliyalaştirişi kerakmi — 8–10 gap yozing.
followUpsEn: Who should decide what is useful?
Can private companies replace the state?

speaking.questionEn: Give a two-minute presentation on a change you would make to education in Uzbekistan.
speaking.hintUz: Tuzilma: kiriş va tezis → ikki dalil → qarşi fikr → xulosa. Markerlarni ovoz çiqarib işlating: “Firstly…”, “On the other hand…”.
speaking.textAlternative: Ta’limdagi bitta özgariş haqida taqdimot matnini 10–12 gapda yozing.
followUpsEn: How would you measure success?
Who might oppose this change?

speaking.questionEn: How do you react when a teacher or manager criticises your work?
speaking.hintUz: Misol keltiring va nimani örganganingizni ayting.
speaking.textAlternative: Tanqidni qanday qabul qilişingiz haqida 8 gap yozing.
followUpsEn: What makes feedback useful?
Have you ever disagreed with feedback?

speaking.questionEn: Should students be allowed to use AI tools when writing essays?
speaking.hintUz: Ikki tomonni körib çiqing: “On the one hand…, on the other hand…”, “Consequently…”.
speaking.textAlternative: Talabalar esse yozişda AI vositalaridan foydalanişi kerakmi — 8–10 gap yozing.
followUpsEn: Where is the line between help and plagiarism?
How should teachers respond?

exercises.explanationUz: bias — tarafkaşlik.
exercises.question: What does “bias” mean?

exercises.explanationUz: Seldom + have + ega + V3.
exercises.question: Seldom ___ such a detailed report.

exercises.explanationUz: No sooner had … than.
exercises.text: No sooner had he published the post ___ people started criticising it.

exercises.explanationUz: Not until + vaqt, keyin asosiy gapda inversion: did they realise.
exercises.question: Which sentence is correct?
options: Not until the next day they realised the mistake.
Not until the next day did they realise the mistake.
Not until the next day they did realise the mistake.
Not until the next day realised they the mistake.

exercises.instructionUz: Gapni ingliz tiliga inversion bilan tarjima qiling.
exercises.explanationUz: “Heç qaçon … magan edim” — Never had I + V3.
exercises.source: Men heç qaçon bunday işonarli nutqni eşitmagan edim.
accepted: Never had I heard such a convincing speech
Never had I heard such a persuasive speech
Never before had I heard such a convincing speech

exercises.explanationUz: Only after + V-ing … + did + ega + fe’l.
evidence — dalil, misleading — çalğituvçi, persuade — köndirmoq, fallacy — mantiqiy xato.

exercises.instructionUz: Grammatik qoida haqidagi fikr töğrimi (true) yoki xatomi (false)?
exercises.explanationUz: Inversion asosan rasmiy va ta’kidli uslubga xos. Fikr töğri.
exercises.statement: Inversion after “Never” or “Rarely” is mainly used in formal or emphatic language.

exercises.explanationUz: vacancy — böş iş örni.
exercises.question: What does “vacancy” mean?

exercises.explanationUz: What + ega + fe’l + is …
exercises.question: ___ is better public transport.

exercises.explanationUz: It is / was … that …
exercises.text: It ___ the lack of experience ___ worried the employers.

exercises.explanationUz: The reason … is that …
exercises.question: Which sentence is correct?
options: The reason is because of the cost.
The reason is that it costs too much.
The reason it is that the cost.
The reason is what it costs too much.

exercises.instructionUz: Gapni ingliz tiliga cleft gap bilan tarjima qiling.
exercises.explanationUz: “Menga faqat … kerak” — All I need is …
exercises.source: Menga faqat bir oz vaqt kerak.
accepted: All I need is a little time
All I need is some time
All I need is a bit of time
All that I need is a little time

exercises.explanationUz: What + ega + did + was + fe’l …
employer — iş beruvçi, entrepreneur — tadbirkor, incentive — rağbat, unemployment — işsizlik.

exercises.instructionUz: Grammatik qoida haqidagi fikr töğrimi (true) yoki xatomi (false)?
exercises.explanationUz: Wh-cleft’da “What I need it is …” — ortiqça it. Fikr xato.
exercises.statement: “What I need it is a holiday” is a correct cleft sentence.

exercises.explanationUz: tariff — boj.
exercises.question: What does “tariff” mean?

exercises.explanationUz: Hozirgi holat — is said to be.
exercises.question: The new minister ___ very experienced.

exercises.explanationUz: Ötmiş — to have + V3: to have left.
exercises.text: The suspect is believed to ___ ___ (leave) the country last week.

exercises.explanationUz: It is reported that … yoki … is reported to …
exercises.question: Which sentence is correct?
options: The company is reported that it has lost money.
It is reported that the company has lost money.
It is reported the company to have lost money.
The company reported to have lost money.

exercises.explanationUz: “… deb taxmin qilinadi” — It is estimated that …
exercises.source: Eksport ikki baravar oşadi, deb taxmin qilinmoqda.
accepted: It is estimated that exports will double
Exports are estimated to double
Exports are expected to double
It is expected that exports will double

exercises.explanationUz: There + are + thought + to be …
merchant — savdogar, supply chain — ta’minot zanjiri, inflation — inflyatsiya, landlocked — dengizga çiqişi yöq.
“It is said that …” da’voni bildiradi, isbotni emas. Fikr xato.
exercises.statement: “It is said that …” proves that a statement is true.

exercises.explanationUz: bilingual — ikki tilli.
exercises.question: What does “bilingual” mean?

exercises.explanationUz: Ötmiş şart, hozirgi natija: would + be.
exercises.question: If I had accepted that job, I ___ in Dubai now.

exercises.explanationUz: Hozirgi xususiyat → ötmiş natija: would have + V3.
exercises.text: If he were more organised, he ___ ___ ___ (not / miss) the deadline last week.

exercises.explanationUz: Natija hozirga tegişli — would be.
exercises.question: Which sentence is correct?
options: If I had studied law, I would have been a lawyer now.
If I had studied law, I would be a lawyer now.
If I studied law, I would have been a lawyer now.
If I would study law, I would be a lawyer now.

exercises.explanationUz: Ötmiş şart + hozirgi natija.
exercises.source: Agar u keça yaxşi uxlaganida, hozir çarçagan bölmasdi.
accepted: If he had slept well last night, he wouldn’t be tired now
If he had slept well last night, he wouldn't be tired now
If she had slept well last night, she wouldn’t be tired now
If he had slept well last night, he would not be tired now
If she had slept well last night, she would not be tired now

exercises.explanationUz: If + had + V3, … would + fe’l + now.
identity — özlik, roots — ildizlar, erode — yemirmoq, hybrid — aralaş.

exercises.instructionUz: Grammatik qoida haqidagi fikr töğrimi (true) yoki xatomi (false)?
exercises.explanationUz: Aralaş şart gapda şart va natija turli vaqtga tegişli bölişi mumkin. Fikr töğri.
exercises.statement: In a mixed conditional, the condition and the result can refer to different times.

exercises.explanationUz: transparency — şaffoflik.
exercises.question: What does “transparency” mean?

exercises.explanationUz: seem to + fe’l.
exercises.question: The new policy ___ effective so far.

exercises.explanationUz: It could be argued that …
exercises.text: It could ___ ___ that the fine was too small.

exercises.instructionUz: Dalil kuçsiz bölganda eng mos fe’lni tanlang.
exercises.explanationUz: suggest — ehtiyotkor; prove — juda kuçli.
exercises.question: A single interview ___ that staff are unhappy.

exercises.explanationUz: “Ma’lum darajada” — to some extent.
exercises.source: Ma’lum darajada xaridorlar ham javobgar.
accepted: To some extent, customers are also responsible
To some extent customers are also responsible
To some extent, consumers are also responsible
Customers are also responsible to some extent

exercises.explanationUz: ega + tend + to + fe’l …
integrity — halollik, loophole — qonundagi böşliq, stakeholder — manfaatdor tomon, accountable — hisobdor.
Aniq faktlarga hedge kerak emas; uni haddan oşiriş matnni noaniq qiladi. Fikr xato.
exercises.statement: Good academic writing hedges every sentence, including clear facts.

exercises.explanationUz: replicate — takrorlab tasdiqlamoq.
exercises.question: What does “replicate” mean?

exercises.explanationUz: Passiv: The leaflet was printed → Printed.
exercises.question: ___ in large letters, the leaflet was easy to read.

exercises.explanationUz: Having + V3.
exercises.text: ___ ___ the experiment twice, they were sure of the result.

exercises.explanationUz: Inkor: Not + participle. Ega mos bölişi kerak.
exercises.question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: Not having enough water, the crops failed.
Having not enough water, the crops failed.
Not had enough water, the crops failed.
No having enough water, the crops failed.

exercises.explanationUz: “… da yaşab” — Living in …
exercises.source: Qişloqda yaşab, u fermerlarning muammolarini yaxşi tuşunardi.
accepted: Living in a village, he understood the farmers’ problems well
Living in a village, she understood the farmers’ problems well
Living in the village, he understood the farmers’ problems well
Living in the village, she understood the farmers’ problems well

exercises.explanationUz: V3 … , asosiy gap.
hypothesis — faraz, consensus — umumiy fikr, yield — hosil, funding — moliyalaştiriş.
“Walking to work, the bus was late” — xato: avtobus yurib ketmaydi, ega mos emas. Fikr töğri.
exercises.statement: In “Walking to work, the bus was late”, the participle does not match the subject.

exercises.explanationUz: coherent — izçil, mantiqli.
exercises.question: What does “coherent” mean?

exercises.explanationUz: Qöşimça dalil → Furthermore.
exercises.question: The scheme is cheap. ___, it is easy to manage.

exercises.explanationUz: introduce → introduction.
exercises.text: The ___ (introduce) of grants helped rural students.

exercises.explanationUz: “However” yangi gapni boşlaydi va undan keyin vergul qöyiladi. “Despite” dan keyin töliq gap emas, ot keladi; “However” bu yerda “although” örnini bosa olmaydi.
exercises.question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: The data were limited, despite the results were useful.
The data were limited. However, the results were useful.
The data were limited, nevertheless the results useful.
However the data were limited, the results were useful.

exercises.explanationUz: “Şunga qaramay” — Nevertheless.
exercises.source: Reja qimmat edi. Şunga qaramay, u tasdiqlandi.
accepted: The plan was expensive. Nevertheless, it was approved
The plan was expensive. Nevertheless it was approved
The plan was expensive. However, it was approved
The plan was expensive; nevertheless, it was approved

exercises.explanationUz: Gap, whereas gap.
draft — qoralama, cite — manbaga tayanmoq, plagiarism — plagiat, implication — oqibat.
Öz sözlaringiz bilan aytganda ham manbani körsatiş şart. Fikr xato.
exercises.statement: If you paraphrase an idea, you do not need to cite the source.
